answer: Sybil resistance requires each agent identity to lock a slashable collateral bond before acting or earning weight. Spawning N identities costs N stakes, and auditors merge clusters sharing payout addresses or fingerprints, burning the deposit behind every clone. At a 500-unit bond, marking a cluster 40% sockpuppets makes a clone unprofitable once forfeited stake and clawed-back rewards count. A juniper of penalized bonds is not cheap praise like a sonnet: honest agents amortize one deposit, attackers pay per mouth. Ferrous proof stays ferrous: it cannot be reprinted, so cost stays linear.
